title: Differences of Mucinous Versus Non-mucinous Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Response
official: Differences of Mucinous Versus Non-mucinous Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Response to Neoadjuvant Treatment and Surgery in a Curative Setting: Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study (the MUNLARC Study)
summary:
Mucinous cell adenocarcinoma of the rectum is a histopathological subtype of rectal cancer first described in 1923 and characterised by the presence of mucin-producing tumour cells in the rectum, with extracellular mucin representing more than 50% of the tumour composition. Mucinous rectal adenocarcinomas have a higher tendency to be diagnosed at an advanced stage, metastasise to regional lymph nodes, recur locally, cause peritoneal carcinomatosis, and have a worse prognosis compared to non-mucinous adenocarcinomas.

This multicenter study aims to assess the differences between mucinous and non-mucinous locally advanced rectal cancer responses to the neoadjuvant treatment and surgery in a curative setting. Downstaging differences will be evaluated by comparing the pre-neoadjuvant and post-neoadjuvant magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). In contrast, post-surgical differences will be assessed by comparing the pathological complete response, the tumour regression grade, the radicality of the surgery, the local and distant recurrence risk and the overall and cancer-specific survival.

.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* diagnosis of non-metastatic, non-recurrent, locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the rectum
* undergoing intention-to-treat neoadjuvant therapy and subsequent surgery at the referral centres

Exclusion Criteria:

* All patients with a different histology diagnosis, metastatic or recurrent disease, or undergoing nonintention-to-treat management
* Patients with confirmed metastases at diagnosis to non-regional lymph nodes or other distant organs
* Patients with previous or concurrent malignancies, except for adequately treated basal or squamous cell skin cancer, in situ cervical cancer, or other cancer for which the patient has been disease-free for five years before study entry
